subject: Clarify latency window apportionment for Oct 14 partial degradation
messages:
From: Jeff Reynolds <jeff@aurelia-health.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@aurelia-health.com>, Procurement <procurement@aurelia-health.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Partial latency on Oct 14 — credits and window question

Hi Connor,

We noticed elevated 95th-percentile latency between 09:50 and 10:40 PDT on Oct 14 that impacted two of our customer-facing endpoints. The monitoring team flagged partial request failures where tail latency spiked but service remained responsive for lower-percentile traffic. Your SLA doc references "partial degradation" handling and third-party maintenance exclusions, but the credit calculation we received seems to allocate the whole 50-minute window as outage time. Can you explain how Redwood calculated the uptime deduction?

What we need: a short explanation of the apportionment method and a CSV of the per-minute availability you used so we can reconcile with our telemetry.

Thanks,
Jeff Reynolds
Director, Platform Engineering
Aurelia Health

[Attachment: aurelia_monitoring-sample.log (text) — referenced]

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Jeff Reynolds <jeff@aurelia-health.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partial latency on Oct 14 — credits and window question

Jeff —

Thanks for the prompt note and for attaching the sample log. I'm investigating with our infra team and will share the per-minute tally. Preliminary notes while we dig in:
- Our system considers a minute "degraded" only if error rate or median latency exceeds configured thresholds for that route.
- We also apply a 5-minute dampening window for transient spikes to avoid counting brief blips as full outage minutes.
- Third-party maintenance events (e.g., CDN provider) are classified under exception rules if we can verify the provider's incident overlap.

I'll loop back with the CSV and a short explanation no later than EOD tomorrow. If you can share the exact route names (internal to your SRE) that saw the spike, that helps map metrics.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Partial latency on Oct 14 — credits and window question

Connor / Vivek —

I pulled the telemetry and attached a per-minute tally (see attachment stub below). Observations:
- From 09:50–09:59 the error rate rose above 2.5% for one route; median latency was within SLO.
- 10:00–10:25 shows sustained 95th percentile latency > 800ms on two routes; error rate stayed ~1%.
- 10:26–10:40 contains falling latency but intermittent spikes.

How we typically handle apportionment for mixed conditions: we mark minutes as "degraded" when either:
  * error rate threshold exceeded, OR
  * sustained P95 above configured latency threshold for that route for >3 minutes after dampening.
We then apply the 5-minute dampening to prevent counting a minute if it immediately follows a restored minute.

Question for Vivek: there is an overlapping maintenance window reported by our CDN partner from 10:10–10:20. Do we treat that as an exception that removes those minutes entirely from Aurelia's uptime tally, or do we only exclude minutes where the CDN provides an incident ID that maps to the affected edge region?

Attachments: uptime_tally-2026-10-14.csv (summary per-minute)

- Marissa

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Jeff Reynolds <jeff@aurelia-health.com>, Procurement <procurement@aurelia-health.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2026 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partial latency on Oct 14 — credits and window question

Jeff —

Appreciate your patience while we reconciled this. Summary of outcome and next steps:

1) What we found
- Our per-minute tally (attached) classifies the 09:50–10:40 window as: 09:50–09:59 (minor error spike), 10:00–10:09 (server-side P95 latency), 10:10–10:20 (edge CDN reported maintenance), 10:21–10:40 (residual tail spikes).
- Under our SLA rules, minutes attributed to third-party provider maintenance are excluded from Redwood's uptime denominator only when the provider supplies an incident ID that maps to the affected region and our routing shows a >30% request path incidence to that provider. The CDN supplied an incident bulletin but did not include region-level mapping; therefore we cannot fully exclude 10:10–10:20 automatically.

2) Proposed apportionment (attached spreadsheet)
- We propose counting 09:50–09:59 and 10:00–10:09 as degraded (fully counted against Redwood).
- For 10:10–10:20 we propose a partial apportionment: per-minute weighting based on request path mapping. In this case the mapping shows ~45% of affected traffic traversed the CDN edge currently under maintenance, so we allocate 45% of those minutes as third-party-exception and 55% as Redwood-impact minutes.
- 10:21–10:40 remains Redwood-impact minutes where P95 exceeded threshold intermittently; we treat them as degraded minutes after dampening rules.

3) Credit calculation and next steps
- Based on the above, the proposed credit is a partial credit equating to 17 minutes of Redwood-impact (out of the 50 total), which matches the attached proposed-apportionment.xlsx.
- If Aurelia can provide a region-mapped incident ID from the CDN or independent routing logs showing >60% of requests on the affected path, we will re-evaluate and can increase the excluded minutes proportionally.

Please see the attached CSV and spreadsheet for the detailed per-minute numbers. Happy to hop on a quick call if you'd like to walk the numbers together; propose Thu 10/30 10:00 PT.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
